66144-milk-run.title: Milk Run
66144-milk-run.creator: Unknown
66144-milk-run.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. He growled, "Blast off, Mr. Blast off!"  "Aye aye, sir," Guhn paused, then reported: "I thought you should know, Captain. We just brought on some skags. Some archeology outfit's shipping the things to Earth for further study."  "Blasted mummies. Next, we'll be hauling heathen idols." Captain Warren glanced at his chronometer. "Shove-off time, is it? Go to the bridge and tell Mr. Caldwell I said to make her grunt."  This was his final utterance.

arxiv-2112-05468.title: Taking advantage of sampling designs in Bayesian spatial small area survey studies.
arxiv-2112-05468.creator: Carlos Vergara-Hernández, Marc Marí-Dell’Olmo, Laura Oliveras, Miguel A. Martinez-Beneito
arxiv-2112-05468.description: Abstract Spatial small area estimation models have become very popular in some contexts, such as disease mapping. Data in disease mapping studies are exhaustive, that is, the available data are supposed to be a complete register of all the observable events.

arxiv-2210-01803.title: Federated Graph-based Networks with Shared Embedding
arxiv-2210-01803.creator: Tianyi Yu, Pei Lai, Fei Teng
arxiv-2210-01803.description: Abstract Nowadays, user privacy is becoming an issue that cannot be bypassed for system developers, especially for that of web applications where data can be easily transferred through internet. Thankfully, federated learning proposes an innovative method to train models with distributed devices while data are kept in local storage.

arxiv-2305-12930.title: Pattern reconstruction through generalized eigenvectors on defective networks
arxiv-2305-12930.creator: Marie Dorchain, Riccardo Muolo, Timoteo Carletti
arxiv-2305-12930.description: Abstract Self-organization in natural and engineered systems causes the emergence of ordered spatio-temporal motifs. In presence of diffusive species, Turing theory has been widely used to understand the formation of such patterns on continuous domains obtained from a diffusion-driven instability mechanism.

arxiv-2506-17590.title: DRAMA-X: A Fine-grained Intent Prediction and Risk Reasoning Benchmark For Driving
arxiv-2506-17590.creator: Mihir Godbole, Xiangbo Gao, Zhengzhong Tu
arxiv-2506-17590.description: Abstract Understanding the short-term motion of vulnerable road users (VRUs) like pedestrians and cyclists is critical for safe autonomous driving, especially in urban scenarios with ambiguous or high-risk behaviors. While vision-language models (VLMs) have enabled open-vocabulary perception, their utility for fine-grained intent reasoning remains underexplored.

arxiv-2507-01174.title: Entanglement on a Sphere
arxiv-2507-01174.creator: K. Boutivas, D. Katsinis, G. Pastras, N. Prountzos, and N. Tetradis
arxiv-2507-01174.description: Abstract We study the entanglement entropy of a massive scalar field in the background of the Einstein universe. We determine numerically the structure of the UV-divergent terms. We study analytically the IR term that originates in the long-range correlations arising from the field zero mode on the sphere.

pmc-11493408.title: DGRPool, a web tool leveraging harmonized Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel phenotyping data for the study of complex traits
pmc-11493408.creator: Vincent Gardeux, Roel PJ Bevers, Fabrice PA David, Emily Rosschaert, Romain Rochepeau, Bart Deplancke, Jonathan Flint, Vincent Gardeux, Roel PJ Bevers, Fabrice PA David, Emily Rosschaert, Romain Rochepeau, Bart Deplancke
pmc-11493408.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Genome-wide association studies have advanced our understanding of complex traits, but studying how a GWAS variant can affect a specific trait in the human population remains challenging due to environmental variability. Drosophila melanogaster is in this regard an excellent model organism for studying the relationship between genetic and phenotypic variation due to its simple handling, standardized growth conditions, low cost, and short lifespan.

pmc-11510547.title: Optimization of the Cold Water Extraction Method for High-Value Bioactive Compounds from Chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla L.) Flower Heads Through Chemometrics
pmc-11510547.creator: Martina Foschi, Lorenzo Marsili, Ilaria Luciani, Giulia Gornati, Claudia Scappaticci, Fabrizio Ruggieri, Angelo Antonio D’Archivio, Alessandra Biancolillo
pmc-11510547.description: This study focused on optimizing a cold water extraction method to obtain bioactive compounds from chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla L.), addressing increasing consumer demand for natural products and nutraceuticals. A full-factorial design was employed to evaluate the effects of temperature, time, and chamomile amount on the polyphenolic profile of extracts.

pmc-12495665.title: Development and validation of a nomogram for predicting high-risk pathology in clinical stage lA left upper lobe lung adenocarcinoma
pmc-12495665.creator: Defeng Luo, Kunsong Su, Yu Han, Qiduo Yu, Hongxiang Feng, Chaoyang Liang, Weijie Zhu
pmc-12495665.description: BackgroundAccurate preoperative identification of high-risk pathological features in early-stage lung adenocarcinoma is critical for guiding surgical decisions and improving patient outcomes. This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram to predict high-risk pathology in clinical stage IA lung adenocarcinoma located in the left upper lobe (LUL), an anatomical site with distinct surgical implications.

pmc-12595820.title: Acquisition of respiratory surface EMG: a systematic literature review of electrode configurations and methodological reporting
pmc-12595820.creator: R S P Warnaar, J E Francovich, L van Baaren, D W Donker, A H Jonkman, E Oppersma
pmc-12595820.description: BackgroundMechanical ventilation provides life-saving support to patients with respiratory failure, but inadequately tailored settings can lead to respiratory muscle dysfunction and poor patient outcomes. Surface electromyography (sEMG) offers a non-invasive modality to monitor respiratory muscle function. However, variability in acquisition setups limits the comparability of study findings and hinders broad clinical implementation.

pmc-12618105.title: A rare case of bacterial translocation from a renal abscess resulting in empyema necessitans: a case report and literature review
pmc-12618105.creator: Monica Bobila, Walid Akram Hussain, Niyousha Ahmadi, Gregory Crisafulli, Aakash Trivedi, Vinay Tak
pmc-12618105.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Empyema necessitans (EN) is a rare complication of thoracic empyema in which infection spreads into the chest wall. While historically associated with tuberculosis, EN caused by Escherichia coli is exceedingly rare. Our report highlights a case of EN in a 76-year-old male that developed after dislodgement of a chest tube placed for the treatment of a pleural effusion associated with a perinephric abscess.

pmc-12727184.title: Estimating risk of reported versus theoretical drug-drug interactions in headaches medicine: an exhaustive comparison between DrugBank and FAERS database for abortive and preventive combinations
pmc-12727184.creator: Victor Kaytser, Ian Hakkinen, Jay Dave, Pengfei Zhang
pmc-12727184.description: Background: Polypharmacy is common in headache medicine. This project uses DrugBank and Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) to determine the likelihood of a theoretical and empirically reported interaction between a given number of headache abortive and preventive medications.

pmc-12787362.title: Distribution Characteristics and Adaptation Mechanisms of Exotic Spontaneous Plant Diversity in Urban Road Green Spaces of Changchun, China
pmc-12787362.creator: Diyang Liu, Congcong Zhao, Yongfang Wang, Yuandong Hu
pmc-12787362.description: Spontaneous plants are plants that occur in urban environments such as pavement gaps or cracks in walls without cultivation and are not remnants of historic native habitats. They are critical components of urban road green space vegetation, and their distribution is affected by multiple factors. Heavy traffic and frequent human disturbances on urban roads exacerbate exotic spontaneous plant invasions.

pmc-13035859.title: A Case Report of Loperamide-Induced Respiratory Depression in Severe Gastrointestinal Inflammation Secondary to Chemotherapy
pmc-13035859.creator: Joanne Yuen Heng Thong, Rajkumar Satyavolu
pmc-13035859.description: Under normal circumstances, loperamide has minimal systemic absorption due to extensive first-pass metabolism and limited permeability across the intestinal mucosa. However, in the presence of severe gastrointestinal inflammation, compromised mucosal integrity may enhance loperamide’s central opioid effects via altered pharmacokinetics. Although respiratory depression due to therapeutic loperamide use remains sparse, this case accentuates the risks in vulnerable patients.

pmc-13230814.title: Target trial emulation of early acetaminophen use and mortality in critically ill stroke patients
pmc-13230814.creator: Xinyan Wang, Kangda Zhang, Youxuan Wu, Zihui Zhang, Yang Li, Ruquan Han, Fa Liang
pmc-13230814.description: The role of acetaminophen in managing critically ill patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is debated. While it is commonly used for fever and pain, its direct impact on mortality in the intensive care unit (ICU) setting is unclear. This study aims to estimate the causal effect of early acetaminophen administration on mortality in critically ill adults with AIS.

pmc-13280299.title: Calculating the Probability that a Previously Susceptible Individual is Infected as a Function of Time Following Exposure to SARS-CoV-2
pmc-13280299.creator: Alun Thomas, Karim Khader, Adam Hersh, Matthew Samore
pmc-13280299.description: IntroductionReliable assessment of disease state probabilities for an individual following a specific exposure event, such as an occupational exposure, is critical for managing isolation and quarantine and reducing onward transmission to susceptible individuals. Such assessments are particularly important for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), where infection, testing, and infectiousness vary substantially across individuals and time since exposure.
